_comment: Context layer vector store on Pinecone, implementing schemas/vector/metadata-contract.md. This file is documentation shaped as data: 'index' is the create-index request, 'metadata_schema' lists the fields every vector carries, and the two examples show an upsert and a filtered query. Placeholders are in angle brackets; vectors are truncated to three numbers and carry 1536 in practice. Fictional tenants only (Globex Logistics is CLIENT-001).

index._comment: Serverless index. One index for the whole context layer; tenants are separated by namespace (below). Cosine metric to match the other stores in this folder. Dimension must equal the embedding model's output and is fixed at creation: changing models means a new index and a full re-embed.
index.name: context-layer

namespaces._comment: One namespace per tenant_id, named exactly as the tenant_id ('company' for the single-company pattern, the client contract's client_id such as 'CLIENT-001' for a consultancy). A query runs inside one namespace, so a tenant cannot be reached by forgetting a filter; the tenant_id metadata field is still written and filtered on (rule 1) as the second lock. Audience is decided per index, not per namespace: an index that client users can query holds only client_shared and public chunks; client_private chunks for the delivery team go in a separate index (or are not embedded). Delete a tenant by deleting its namespace at offboarding.

vector_id._comment: Deterministic id: {source_system}:{source_id}#{chunk_index}. Re-ingestion is an upsert. Serverless indexes delete by id or by whole namespace, not by metadata filter, so to remove one page list the ids by prefix ('notion:p-readme#') and delete that list. That is why the id starts with the source, not with a random uuid.

metadata_schema._comment: Every metadata field is filterable on a serverless index, so keep the set flat and small (40 KB per vector including the text). Pinecone metadata has no null: omit canonical_slug for depth sources instead of writing null. Timestamps are stored twice: ISO 8601 string for display, epoch seconds as a number for range filters ($gte, $lt). 'embedding' is the vector's values, not metadata; 'id' is the vector id, not metadata.

fields.name: tenant_id
fields.why: Isolation key, equal to the namespace name. Filtered on every query even though the namespace already isolates it.

fields.name: source_system
fields.why: Where the chunk came from; lets a query restrict to canon pages.

fields.name: source_id
fields.why: Page, file or record id; with source_system identifies the source for replace-and-delete.

fields.name: source_url
fields.why: The citation returned with every match.

fields.name: canonical_slug
fields.why: Contract slug for canonical pages; omitted (not null) for depth sources.

fields.name: status
fields.why: Copied from the contract. Queries default to grounded; deprecated chunks are deleted, never present.

fields.name: visibility
fields.why: Copied from the contract. Filtered with $in against the caller's scope.

fields.name: content_hash
fields.why: sha256 hex of text. Dedupe lookup before embedding.

fields.name: chunk_index
fields.why: Position within the source; enables neighbour expansion.

fields.name: text
fields.why: The chunk content, returned with the match so no second fetch is needed. Counts toward the 40 KB metadata limit.

fields.name: token_count
fields.why: Tokens in text, for prompt budgeting.

fields.name: generated_at
fields.why: ISO 8601; when the content last changed. A moved generated_at means the source's chunks are replaced.

fields.name: generated_at_epoch
fields.why: Same clock as a number so range filters work.

fields.name: last_synced_at_epoch
fields.why: Heartbeat as a number; max per namespace is the tenant's freshness.

fields.name: heading_path
fields.why: Extras from the metadata object are flattened to top-level keys because Pinecone metadata is flat. Never secrets, never personal data.

example_upsert._comment: One vector per chunk, upserted into the tenant's namespace. values is truncated here.

metadata.text: Client README > Who we are. Globex Logistics engagement readme, chunk 0 ...

example_query._comment: Rule 1 in Pinecone terms: namespace = tenant, and the filter names tenant_id, visibility and status every time. The retrieval service builds the filter from the caller's identity; the prompt never sees it. Read source_url from each match's metadata and cite it.

example_delete_source._comment: Removing a deprecated or changed page: list ids by prefix inside the namespace, then delete them. Run this before inserting the new chunks of a changed page so a query never sees old and new together.

freshness._comment: Pinecone has no aggregate query. Keep the per-tenant heartbeat where the sync writes it (export/meta.json or a small table) and check it before querying; or query the namespace for one vector with includeMetadata and read last_synced_at_epoch from any chunk, since the sync updates all chunks of a tenant in one run.
